sentences.text: (By Smt. Ekta Gupta - Panel Lawyer)

This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the
following:
 Order

This is second application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.09/2023 dated 03.01.2023 registered at Police Station Pali, district Umaria, for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)
(n) and 376(3) of IPC and Sections 5r/w 6 and 5(j)(ii)/6 of the POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 24.01.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He also submits that applicant is a permanent resident of district Umaria and is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
This is second bail application filed by the applicant.
His earlier one was dismissed on merits vide order dated 12.6.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.22881/2023 by this Court.

The prosecutrix had complained that she was raped by the applicant after administering her some drug and later she was repeatedly sexually abused by the applicant who was black-mailing her on the basis of some obscene photographs and videos of her.
The mobile phone of applicant was seized but no photographs or videos have been retrieved from its data to be filed along with the charge-sheet.
The prosecutrix has been examined before the trial court in which she has not stated any incriminating fact against the applicant.
In fact, she has not even identified the applicant during her court testimony.

Looking to these change in the circumstances, this Court deems it proper to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this second bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE ps Date: 2023.07.24 14:55:30 +05'30'
